messages:
Jules (CEO): Kicking off the runtime/stack Q&A from today's all-hands — drop questions about batching, caching, kernel work, or rollout plans here and we'll answer live.

Avery (Eng Dir): Slides + short roadmap are at https://redwood.internal/s/allhands-runtime (see 'Runtime perf' section). Will try to answer most here, follow-ups welcome.

Priya (Runtime): Quick question: what are we prioritizing for KV cache in the next quarter? Is the plan to make it LRU+prefetch or something different?

Avery (Eng Dir): Short answer: LRU baseline + adaptive prefix prefetching. Long answer: we want deterministic cache eviction per customer partition + a prefetch policy that learns common prefixes for chat sessions. Goal: reduce repeated token compute and cold-starts for multi-turn.

Diego (ML Infra): What's the expected latency impact from the batching changes we've been prototyping? Any numbers?

Avery (Eng Dir): From internal bench: switching to continuous batching with small batch windows (6-12ms) + dynamic batch sizing gave ~1.15x p50 improvement for short requests (<=128 tokens) and up to 1.6x throughput improvement under bursty load, with p99 staying within SLO in our tests.

Maya (Product): For customers worried about QoE, how will canaries/fallbacks work when we change kernels or enable quantization by default?

Avery (Eng Dir): Canary per-customer flag. We'll run A/B for 1-5% of traffic, compare quality metrics (per our eval harness) + latency/cost metrics. Automatic fallback to previous kernel/model variant on quality regressions. Rollouts gated by eval/alert rules.

Priya (Runtime): Can you share the experimental config we used? paste for ops folks.

Avery (Eng Dir): Sure — example config we used in bench:
```
batching: 
  enabled: true
  batch_window_ms: 8
  max_batch_size: 128
  dynamic_scale: true
kv_cache: 
  mode: partitioned
  eviction: lru
  prefetch: adaptive
kernel: 
  fused_attention: auto
  quantization: int8_delta
```

Diego (ML Infra): Thanks — that matches what we ran. One note: int8_delta is still experimental on A100; perf gains vary by sequence length.

Priya (Runtime): Are we planning to surface recommended defaults in the Console Optimize tab? Customers keep asking for prescriptive settings.

Avery (Eng Dir): Yes — Optimize will ship presets next sprint: 'low-latency', 'cost-efficient', 'throughput-optimized' with suggested batch_window_ms, cache_policy, and quantization profile. Each preset will show expected tradeoffs.

Diego (ML Infra): Kernel work update: kernel team is landing a fused attention kernel next month for short-seq models — internally we see 2-3x token/sec improvement at seq<=128 vs baseline. Longer sequences still use block-sparse/standard paths.

Maya (Product): Any change to API contract customers should worry about?

Avery (Eng Dir): No breaking API changes. We may add new params (e.g., batching hints) but defaults keep behavior stable.

Priya (Runtime): SLA-wise — does dedicated capacity get these optimizations automatically or is it opt-in?

Avery (Eng Dir): Dedicated clusters will get the runtime updates via rolling upgrade. Customers can opt-out per cluster if they need a frozen stack for certification.

ops-bot: deploy/12345 started to runtime-canary (region: us-west-2) by ci-system — ETA ~7m :rocket:

Diego (ML Infra): One operational caveat: continuous batching increases GPU memory pressure due to larger aggregate KV caches; we'll be tuning prefetch sizes per-model to cap memory.

Priya (Runtime): Cool — can we get a follow-up thread with the pref thresholds per model family? I'll collect a few examples.

Avery (Eng Dir): Yes — I'll create an eng-runtime doc with per-model knobs and add benchmarks. Thanks for the great questions. :thumbsup:

Jules (CEO): Thanks everyone — appreciate the concrete numbers. We'll share a short post-all-hands summary with links to the deploy and the eng doc.

Maya (Product): Adding action items: 1) eng-runtime doc + knobs (Avery) 2) Console presets (Product + DevEx) 3) Customer comms template for Dedicated opt-out (Customer Success).

Priya (Runtime): Thanks — will follow up on the pref thresholds.

Avery (Eng Dir): Marking this closed for now; feel free to reopen with follow-ups.
